relevance_note: Cohort patient P6 carries a de novo 3.576 Mb 6q23.3-q24.1 deletion: "The TNFAIP3 gene was involved in the deleted fragment in P6".
method_note: Read the full paper manually; a short Python script assembled the JSON, cut patients-as-columns table spans (Tables 1 and 2, column header '| Patient | P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 | P5 | P6'; P6 is the sixth patient column) and the Table 3 row segment, and verified every span verbatim (the paper uses non-breaking spaces and en dashes). Scope: this is a 145-patient FUO cohort with chromosomal abnormalities (P1-P8) plus a literature table of 19 patients; only P6 (de novo 3.576 Mb 6q23.3-q24.1 deletion including TNFAIP3) and the Table 3 literature patient '6q23.2-q24.3 del' (ref [18], whose title names TNFAIP3 haploinsufficiency in a patient with a 13Mb chromosome 6 deletion) relate to TNFAIP3, so only they and P6's tested parents ('Father', 'mother' in the Fig. 4a legend) were extracted; P1-P5, P7, P8 and the other 18 literature patients have no TNFAIP3 variant per the paper and were not extracted. The link between the Table 3 row and TNFAIP3 rests on the reference [18] title and the TNFAIP3 discussion paragraph, not on an explicit statement in the main text. Rule 6 applied: Table 1 and Table 3 use '+'/'–', and '–' cells were treated as not reported, not excluded; exclusions for P6 (pharyngitis/tonsillitis, oral ulcers) come only from text naming the affected subset of the six inflammatory-fever patients ('4/6 patients (P1-P4)'; 'oral aphthous ulcer (2/6)' with '(P4 and P5)'). Hyperpyrexia for P6 comes from a statement about 'These patients' (P1-P6). P6 pancytopenia is attributed to suspected HLH, not autoimmunity, so the checklist item 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' was left not reported. Seizures (Table 1 only) were taken as CNS involvement. For the literature patient, perianal ulcers (with diarrhoea) were taken as gastrointestinal ulcers; developmental delay was not taken as CNS involvement. P6 age at last evaluation was set to the age at death (4.5 years); Table 2 labs were taken at '51 m' and Table 1 age at diagnosis is 45 m; s-JIA was suspected at 3.6 years. n_patients_reported left null because the authors give no count of TNFAIP3 patients. IFNGR1 is also in P6's deleted region (same CNV, not a separate variant row); P5's PTPN11 variant belongs to a non-TNFAIP3 patient and was not recorded. Inconsistencies noted: the text says CNVs were 'verified with CGH (Fig. 3) or MLPA (Fig. 4c)', but Fig. 3 lists no CGH result for P6 and Fig. 4 says 'P6 by NGS', so orthogonal confirmation of P6's deletion is unclear; Fig. 5 says '6q23.3-24.1 del' occurred in both this and previous studies, whereas the literature deletion is 6q23.2-q24.3; the Discussion gives 24.1% (35/145) monogenic autoinflammatory diagnoses versus 33.1% (48/145) single-gene PID in Results (not patient-level).
